data.hypothesis: Parallelizing the independent per-option loop should improve throughput on large inputs while preserving each option's baseline arithmetic and operation order. Limiting the team to the positive run thread budget and input count avoids excess workers; keeping small counts out of a multi-thread team should reduce launch overhead. These effects remain to be measured.
data.notes: The serial baseline is valid and correct, with mean 0.390079 seconds across three samples. No candidate measurements are available yet, so neither speedup nor small-input overhead is established. The OpenMP condition avoids a multi-thread team below 128 elements, though serialized OpenMP runtime overhead may remain. The controller should measure performance and verify correctness, full output overwrite, and the input/thread cases.
transformations: Parallelize the per-option loop with an OpenMP static worksharing loop when count is at least 128 and more than one thread is available.
Bound the OpenMP team size by the positive run threads argument and count; use one thread for nonpositive counts.
Move the binomial scratch array into the loop body so each iteration has private scratch state, retaining the baseline arithmetic and operation order.
